    <item>
      <title>Braathen med ny maktdemonstrasjon: – Jeg er så full av følelser</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/braathen-med-ny-maktdemonstrasjon_-_-jeg-er-sa-full-av-folelser-1.18082207</link>
      <description>Norsk-brasilianske Lucas Pinheiro Braathen (26) fortsetter å ydmyke konkurrentene.
Etter seier i storslalåm-starten i Sölden, fortsatte han med seier i slalåm i finske Levi søndag.
– Det er så godt å være her i Levi. Jeg er så full av følelser nå. Jeg skal prøve å ta selvtilliten med meg videre til neste renn, sier Braathen selv i arenaintervjuet.
Clément Noël ble nummer to, 56 hundredeler bak vinneren. Atle Lie McGrath ble beste norske på 7. plass.
– Det er hans bakke. Han elsker den. Han elsker disse forholdene, sier TV 2-ekspert Kjetil Jansrud på direkten.
– Han er fremdeles norsk, men han representerer Brasil. Vi skulle gjerne ha sett det norske flagget bak navnet hans, fortsetter Jansrud.
Dette er den tredje vinteren der Braathen representerer Brasil etter at han brøt med Norges Skiforbund.
– For en kjøring. Det er store, store avstander i en bakke som Levi, sa TV 2-ekspert Jansrud etter Braathens første omgang.
Han ledet med hele 65 hundredeler til toeren, Clément Noël, før finaleomgangen.

– Det Lucas gjør det er helt i egen klasse, sa Timon Haugan til TV 2 etter første omgang.
– Jeg fikk meg en på tygga, sier McGrath om finaleomgangen.
Oscar Andreas Sandvik kjørte seg opp fra 29. plass til nummer 11.

    <item>
      <title>Vind og kaos-skyting: Kirkeeide vant fellesstarten etter åtte (!) bom</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/vind-og-kaos-skyting_-kirkeeide-vant-fellesstarten-etter-atte-___-bom-1.18082184</link>
      <description>Maren Kirkeeide stakk av med seieren på kvinnenes fellesstart i skiskyting på Geilo søndag.
Lørdagens sprintsensasjon Guro Ytterhus imponerte igjen og tok andreplass 14,4 sekunder bak Kirkeeide.
Juni Arnekleiv ledet etter to fulle hus, men på tredje skyting ble det kaos. Sterk vind gjorde at flere av utøverne bommet mange ganger, og Arnekleiv røk på fire bom.
Dermed tok Karoline Knotten over teten. Men på siste skyting, så haglet skuddene utenfor blinkene nok en gang.
Og plutselig var Kirkeeide i tet etter hele åtte (!) bom. Få løpere måtte ut i flere strafferunder, men likevel holdt hun ledelsen helt til mål.
– Det var en merkelig fellesstart. Det var veldig mange som bommet. Det var tydeligvis ikke så lett som man skulle tro, sier Kirkeeide til NRK etter seieren.
Karoline Knotten tok tredjeplass.
Ingrid Landmark Tandrevold, Marthe Kråkstad Johansen, Karoline Knotten og nevnte Kirkeeide er forhåndsuttatt til verdenscupstarten i finske Kontiolahti senere i måneden. Kvinnenes tropp skal til slutt bestå av seks løpere.</description>

      <description>USAs transportminister Sean Duffy sier utskiftning av en kobbertråd kan være årsaken til den omfattende flystansen fredag.
Flere enn 15.000 flygninger ble forsinket eller innstilt da amerikanske luftfartsmyndigheter FAA i fire timer nektet alle fly å ta av på grunn av forstyrrelser i flykontrollen.
På en pressekonferanse lørdag sa transportminister Duffy at problemene kan ha oppstått som følge av arbeidet med å bytte ut gamle kobberkabler med fiber ved et av FAAs anlegg.
Ministeren oppgav også navnet på selskapet han mente hadde forsårsaket problemene. Hendelsen skal granskes videre.
Det er fremdeles etterslep etter fredagens problemer. Lørdag er flere enn 10.000 flygninger innstilt eller forsinket, ifølge FlightAware.</description>

      <description>Det brenner kraftig i en enebolig på en gård i Trondheimsveien i Lillestrøm.
– Det er full fyr i hele bygningen, opplyser oppdragsleder i politiet, Ronny Mangseth.
– Brannvesenet er fremme og er i gang med slukking. Det er kontroll på alle fire beboere på stedet, sier han.
Ved 17:20-tiden opplyser politiet at det fortsatt brenner i boligen, og at arbeidet med slukking vil ta tid.
En person skal ha fått i seg noe røyk.
Det skal ikke være fare for spredning til låve eller andre bygninger på gården.
Ifølge politiet er det ikke kjent hva som er årsaken til brannen, og de vil etterforske saken videre.</description>

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/solbakken-overrasker-_-aasgaard-inn-i-startelleveren-1.18081988</link>
      <description>Ståle Solbakken har valgt ut følgende ellever til kampen mot Wales på Ullevaal:
Egil Selvik – Julian Ryerson, Kristoffer Ajer, Torbjørn Heggem, David Møller Wolfe – Sander Berge, Martin Ødegaard, Thelo Aasgaard – Antonio Nusa, Erling Braut Haaland, Oscar Bobb.
– Jeg må innrømme at jeg er noe overrasket. Men da tenker vel Solbakken at han passer bedre til denne kampen enn det Patrick Berg gjør akkurat nå, sier NRK-ekspert Andrine Hegerberg om at Aasgaards inntog i startelleveren.
Han er én av fire bytter som er gjort fra elleveren som møtte Portugal i forrige nasjonsligakamp.
Leo Østigård, Andreas Schjelderup og Patrick Berg er henvist til benken, mens Fredrik Aursnes ikke er med på grunn av en skade.
Samtidig er det nok en gang Egil Selvik som skal vokte buret for Norge.
– Jeg er først og fremst stolt, men også spent. Det blir en viktig kamp for oss, så det gjelder å gi jernet. Vi har noe å revansjere, sier Selvik til TV 2.
På motsatt banehalvdel starter Wales med følgende mannskap:
Karl Darlow – Neco Williams, Joe Rodon, Ben Davies, Jay Dasilva – Harry Wilson, Ethan Ampadu, Liam Cullen, Daniel James – Lewis Koumas, Brennan Johnson.</description>

      <description>Britisk politi bekrefter overfor BBC at de har innledet en etterforskning mot komikeren David Walliams for alvorlige seksuelle forbrytelser.

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/thore-_henki_-holm-hansen-er-dod-1.18081252</link>
      <description>Den tidligere Outlaws-sjefen og countrymusikeren er død, 82 år gammel, melder VG.
Holm Hansen ledet MC-klubben Outlaws, ble dømt for handel med narkotika og våpen og ga ut countrymusikk.
«Han sovnet stille inn på morgenen i dag, hjemme hos meg i sin egen seng, med venner og familie rundt seg», skriver datteren hans June Nordlie i et innlegg på Facebook.
Holm Hansen ble i 1981 dømt til 60 års fengsel i en kokainsak i USA, men ble besluttet deportert til Norge.
Selv hevdet han at dommen var et justismord, og knyttet saken til påstått arbeid for CIA.</description>

      <description>En buss kjørte i dag tidlig av veien i Røn i Vestre Slidre.
Politiet opplyser at bussen skal ha sklidd av veien i lav hastighet, men at den ligger på siden.
Det var tre passasjerer i bussen, alle skolebarn.
Ett barn er kjørt til Gjøvik sykehus for videre kontroll. Øvrige personer er uskadde.
Politiet oppretter sak og bussjåføren er midlertidig fratatt førerkortet.</description>

      <title>Skolebuss av veien i Larvik</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/skolebuss-av-veien-i-larvik-1.18079991</link>
      <description>Nødetatene har fått melding om en skolebuss som har kjørt av veien i Larvik.
– Bussen har sklidd av veien og ut i grøfta med alle fire hjul. I bussen er det 24 barn som fremstår uskadd, skriver operasjonsleder Per Magne Eftang i politiloggen.
Bussjåføren er også uskadd, ifølge politiet.
– Barna er nå på vei ut av bussen og inn et hus for å holde varmen, sier Eftang til NRK.
Han sier alle barna brukte bilbelte.
Operasjonslederen antar at hendelsen kan knyttes til det glatte føret, men politiet har ikke kommet fram til stedet ennå.
Klokka 09.44 opplyser politiet at ingen er skadet. Flere foreldre har hentet barna sine og ny buss er klar til å frakte resten av barna til skolen.</description>

      <title>CNN: Demokratene vinner historisk senatsvalg i Mississippi</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/cnn_-demokratene-vinner-historisk-senatsvalg-i-mississippi-1.18079865</link>
      <description>Demokraten Scott Colom har vunnet senatsvalget i den tradisjonelt republikanske delstaten Mississippi, ifølge CNNs prognose.
Colom slår dermed den sittende republikanske senatoren Cindy Hyde-Smith, melder CNN onsdag kveld.
Han blir den første demokraten som representerer Mississippi i Senatet på over 40 år.
Colom blir også den første svarte politikeren som velges til et politisk verv av velgerne i hele Mississippi siden gjenoppbyggingsperioden etter den amerikanske borgerkrigen på 1800-tallet.
Valget ble holdt 3. november, men opptellingen har trukket ut i over en uke. Onsdag ettermiddag ledet Colom med rundt 3000 stemmer da om lag 98 prosent av stemmene var talt opp.
Resultatet er ennå ikke formelt godkjent. Fylkene i delstaten har frist til fredag med å godkjenne sine valgresultater.
(NTB)</description>

      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/mdg_-vil-fremme-hasteforslag-for-a-pause-gruvesalg-1.18079838</link>
      <description>Miljøpartiet de grønne (MDG) vil fremme et hasteforslag for å få satt kjøpet av Nussir-gruva på vent fram til nødvendige sikkerhetsvurderinger er gjennomført. Det opplyser partiet til NRK.
De reagerer på salget av gruva til et selskap der sjefen hadde tette bånd til folk i Vladimir Putins nære krets.
– Vi ønsker at regjeringa skal pause kjøpet fram til Stortinget eventuelt er overbevist om at dette ikke utgjør et sikkerhetsbrudd, sier Siren Jensen til NRK.
VG omtalte hasteforslaget først.
Nussir-gruva i Finnmark har store mengder kobber, men også gull og sølv.</description>

A Nanaimo store owner who is struggling with nearly daily shoplifting incidents is welcoming the arrests of 17 people in a recent RCMP crackdown. 

The post ‘It is personal’: Nanaimo shop owner welcomes crackdown on shoplifters appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

Setting out new jeans in her Nanaimo boutique on Monday, Jona Kristinsson hoped they would be a big seller.

The owner of Curva-Voom says an increase in shoplifting at her Bowen Road consignment store has cut deep into her profits.

Watch the story below:

Loading the player...

“It is gut-wrenching. It is personal for me when people choose to come into a store like this and steal. And it happens a lot,” says Kristinsson.

The small business owner is now posting surveillance video of people caught shoplifting in her store on social media and says it often helps identify suspects. 

‘It’s tough. It’s tough being in business right now,” says Kristinsson.

The shop owner isn’t alone. According to the Retail Council of Canada, shoplifting costs Canadian businesses over $ 1 billion each year, and it often results in price increases for shoppers down the line.

“They’re taking small items they can convert to buy drugs. That’s the bottom line. It’s the small items. You’re talking meat, because it’s a high-end item, clothing, electronics, anything they can grab,” says Nanaimo RCMP Const. Gary O’Brien.

Nanaimo RCMP executed a two-day blitz targeting shoplifting at Nanaimo’s Port Place Mall and downtown recently. According to O’Brien, on Oct. 19 and 20, it led to 17 arrests and the recovery of $1,500 in stolen property. 

“This is an area that’s being targeted by criminals. It’s like a revolving door. They’re going in, they’re stealing items, they think there’s no accountability; we will put a stop to it,” says O’Brien.

“Every year it’s more and more and more. So it’s reassuring to hear that the RCMP is actually doing something about that,” says Kristinsson.

Kristinsson looks forward to RCMP enforcement teams expanding blitzes on shoplifters to shops across the city.

]]> 1361777 ‘It’s time for them to come back’: Outdoor space hopes to bring new life to Victoria Conservatory https://cheknews.ca/its-time-for-them-to-come-back-outdoor-space-hopes-to-bring-new-life-to-victoria-conservatory-1361772/ Tue, 17 Nov 2026 01:04:36 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1361772

]]>

The Victoria Conservatory of Music unveiled an ongoing outdoor plaza project as the organization returns to full operational capacity.

Not many have been able to set foot in front of Alix Goolden Hall since the pandemic. Security fencing has sectioned off the front doors since 2021.

Watch the story below:

Loading the player...

Five years later, that fencing is getting closer to coming down as part of an outdoor plaza project at the Victoria Conservatory of Music.

“It really wasn’t that long ago that events were happening out here and the city had a vision for this land that it would be a music plaza,” said CEO Nathan Medd.

“These were plans that I inherited four years ago, and the vision never quite got realized.”

In front of the hall sits a modular seating area in the shape of a flower, inspired by the rose window above Alix Goolden Hall. Planter boxes have been installed, and soon, musical notes will be installed along the fence facing Pandora Avenue.

The sculptural music notes are excerpted from a 2022 Chamber opera, Show Room, by two of the conservatory’s alumni, Atom Egoyan and Rodney Sharman.

As the project began, the organization was preparing to reopen Alix Goolden Hall and Wood Recital Hall at full capacity. A third venue, Greenhouse, has been booked to capacity since it opened last month.

Medd says this is the signal he needed to bring back operations to full capacity.

“We think it’s time for them to come back. I wouldn’t say that message if I wasn’t ready to say it, but we weren’t going to say it any sooner than we could have said it.”

The conservatory has faced a tumultuous few years dealing with street disorders, ongoing encampments, bylaw and police enforcement.

“We’ve been looking to this day for a while; we had to close our concert halls at the beginning of the pandemic,” said Medd.

The outdoor plaza project was funded in partnership with the City of Victoria, to the tune of $160,000. The space is located on public property, but Medd says the city has permitted the use of the area for at least a decade.

City Councillor Dave Thompson is looking forward to the future of the conservatory, but says it partly hinges on the province to play its part in deterring street disorder.

“It’s a great vision, and we can probably see that succeeding.”

“Our role is the street, the sidewalk, the infrastructure and then the province plays its role with the health problem,” said Thompson.

Medd adds that neighbours in the area — including Our Place Society — had a say in the project.

“We are imagining the public space we all desire; we all envision something different than what we see out here today,” said the CEO.

The outdoor plaza is expected to be completed by next month. The security fencing in front of Alix Goolden Hall, which has been in place since 2021, will come down in early 2027.

“I’ve seen it four feet higher in the past, about six or seven years ago but this year it’s come up particularly fast,” said Sproat Lake resident Bryce Gibney.

Watch the story below:

Loading the player...

“Usually it takes quite a while for it to come up this high and this year it was just a couple of days, overnight, it came up four or five feet and then it’s just kept on proceeding,” added Doug Herd, the caretaker at Tall Timbers Holiday Park on Lakeshore Road.

Before the latest round of storms, Ward Creek, which runs through Tall Timbers, was dry, but it soon became a torrent of water like many other creeks, which is how the lake filled up so fast.

“Lots of problems, that shed in the distance was on its side this morning, we righted it,” added Herd, who gave CHEK News a tour of the RV park that has shrunk in size due to the rising water.

Homes on the lake that normally have several hundred feet of property now find the lake lapping at their doors.

It’s also causing things like refrigerators to just float away and Herd was dispatched to find one bobbing in the lake today.

He launched his boat in what is normally the parking lot for his boat launch. And the dock for the launch was 50 or so metres out in the water, with the ramp pointing steeply up the dock when it normally points down to it.

“Over the last few years, there hasn’t been that much water; this year it just went nuts,” Herd added.

There are questions around the lake about how to keep water levels from rising so fast.

There is a weir in the Sproat River that empties out of Sproat Lake. In the spring, steel plates are put on top of it to keep water in the lake during the dry summer months.

Those plates were removed Oct. 15. On Monday, the water was rushing down the river at least a metre above the weir.

Residents are now questioning if it can be improved to prevent the lake from getting too high in the winter.

“The lake residents want control over that weir, but there’s always been some argument with the forestry companies and Fisheries as to who’s going to do what when and it doesn’t seem to happen on a timely basis,” Gibney said.

Newly elected regional district director for Area D, Sproat Lake Sabrina Zimmerman, says she brought up the issue at the first meeting.

“I’m planning on looking at other areas like Lake Cowichan that have tried different systems for operating weirs and water flow for their lakes,” she told CHEK News. “Looking for solutions because there’s lots of damage that can happen to people’s properties.”

The water might drop in the next few days. Doug Herd says he’s been told it can go down 30 cm every 24 hours if it doesn’t rain.

Premier-designate Lorne Doerkson may be sworn into office on Friday, but he won’t be immediately recalling the legislature for a fall sitting.

The incoming BC Conservative administration will forgo a two-week sitting of the legislature before Christmas in favour of returning in the spring.

Loading the player...

“Our government has an ambitious agenda, and we want to ensure legislation is properly prepared and receives the debate and consideration it deserves,” Doerkson said Monday.
“Ministers will get to work from day one, advancing our priorities and preparing a substantive legislative agenda for the spring.”

But that does not mean the new government will be unable to enact its agenda in the meantime.

Numerous campaign promises by the Conservatives will only require cabinet orders or ministerial directives to implement, regardless of whether the legislature is in session.

The party’s education agenda is one such example. A pledge to return to singing the national anthem at morning school assemblies is a ministerial directive, as would be restoring letter grades for students in Grades 4 to 7. Eliminating the Sexual Orientation and Gender Identity (SOGI) learning module is another move that does not require legislation.

The Conservatives would not require bills in the house to enact their plan to launch independent reviews of the budget and taxes, nor to reform forestry rules. And high-profile commitments to end the “safe supply” model of government drugs for those suffering from addiction, as well as shut down overdose prevention sites, could similarly be accomplished with cabinet orders.

Doerkson will have to wait until the spring for some other matters, however.

Repealing the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (DRIPA) requires a bill in the house.

And tax measures — from a promised $1,000 income tax rebate to eliminating a PST expansion to restoring below-prime interest rates on seniors’ property tax deferrals — require a budget, which is then debated and passed in the legislature.

The new government could wait until April 30 to introduce a new budget. Doerkson has not said when he will start the spring session of the legislature.

Six years after sounding the alarm over systemic racism within one of British Columbia’s cultural institutions, prominent Haida scholar and former Director of Indigenous Collections Dr. Sdahl Ḵ’awaas (Lucy Bell) is finally receiving a long-awaited formal apology.

For Sdahl Ḵ’awaas and the people of Haida Nation, this moment is about much more than a polished statement on letterhead. In the Haida language, it is about Tll Yahda, which means making things right.

A long road to accountability

The journey to this apology ceremony began in the summer of 2020, when Sdahl Ḵ’awaas left her leadership position as head of Indigenous Collections at the Royal BC Museum (RBCM). She publicly sounded the alarm over racist practices and discrimination directed at herself and other Indigenous staff members. Her resignation in front of staff and museum executives was subsequently leaked to the press.

Watch the story below:

Loading the player...

In her scathing speech, Sdahl Ḵ’awaas called out executives and management during her resignation, telling them they would “hear their own voice” when she gave her resignation speech. Some of the claims Bell made during her speech included citing different conversations that were said to her during her tenure at the museum.

“The Haida cannot pick and choose artifacts for repatriation, they cannot treat this museum like a grocery store. This was in response to the Haida repatriation committee asking for two things out of 2000.” -Sdahl Ḵ’awaas

A year later, an investigative report substantiated Sdahl Ḵ’awaas allegations, confirming that Indigenous staff had faced racism and micro-aggressions within a toxic workplace culture. While the RBCM issued a formal apology at that time, Sdahl Ḵ’awaas and the Haida Nation sought a deeper level of accountability. Through the human rights tribunal process, ongoing conversations and negotiations triggered a crucial ask: a ceremonial apology delivered directly on Haida territory.

That milestone has finally arrived, with three senior RBCM executives, including CEO Allison Bond, travelling to the territory.

Story continues below

Community preparations

Ahead of the ceremony, the atmosphere within Haida Nation is a blend of hope, resilience, and cautious skepticism. At the edge of the world in Haida Gwaii, Haida youth have been putting on regalia and practicing sacred traditional songs and dances that were once broken and lost from the community.

Reflecting on the emotional lead-up to the event, Sdahl Ḵ’awaas shared:

“I was feeling all the emotions getting ready all the lead up to this event has been really beautiful.. really healing… powerful. I’ve been feeling proud and humbled… I experienced and put up with so much racism and to be carrying that all of these years and its been really… its time for me to put this down its time for the museum to properly apologize and properly acknowledge the racism that I went through.” -Sdahl Ḵ’awaas

Master Carver Kihl’yahda (Christian White) expressed strong support for the community coming together around Sdahl Ḵ’awaas and her clan. At the same time, community voices highlighted the ongoing need for genuine structural change.

Candace Weir, Haida community member and cultural guide, has been helping Sdahl Ḵ’awáas prepare for the apology cermony. Weir is sometimes skeptical on colonial institutions intentions and whether or not they turn into tangible actions

“Colonial institutions use words I feel, without actions when you have words that are coin words; it doesn’t align with Indigenous values or indigenous peoples; it’s not practicing what they preach,” said Weir.

Measuring success beyond words

While skepticism can hang heavy in the air, organizers emphasize that the ceremony’s success will not be measured by attendance. Instead, it will be measured in that quiet moment after the final song, when people walk away feeling connected, hopeful, and most importantly, heard.

When asked what she wants to see after the ceremonies conclude, Sdahl Ḵ’awaas emphasized that the museum must fundamentally change how it operates:

“I want to see and hear the museum is committed to healing being and doing better they can’t continue the way they are we can’t continue to be in a relationship when they are so broken.” -Sdahl Ḵ’awaas

As community members work to revive dances and songs that were once lost, many are hoping this apology will leave a lasting change for the museum moving forward.

Robert Pattinson is the next James Bond, and a University of Victoria expert who has spent decades studying the iconic British spy says the casting is a safe choice for a franchise entering a new era.

Early Monday, it was announced that the 40-year-old British actor will take over the role of 007, succeeding Daniel Craig, who last portrayed Bond in 2021’s No Time to Die.

The upcoming film will be directed by Canadian filmmaker Denis Villeneuve, known for Dune and Arrival.

John Threlfall, the University of Victoria’s communications & special projects officer and a longtime Bond enthusiast who taught a course examining the franchise in 2015, says Pattinson’s casting signals a new direction for the series under Amazon’s ownership.

“Traditionally, when it came to casting a new Bond, they never wanted the actor to overshadow the character. So they went with lesser-known actors,” Threlfall told CHEK News.

“Now, for the first time in the history of the character, we’ve got an actor who not only has a huge profile, but he’s also involved with like three other franchises.”

Pattinson is best known for his roles in the Twilight franchise, Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire and The Batman. He is also appearing in Villeneuve’s upcoming Dune: Part Three.

Threlfall believes the decision reflects an effort to attract the widest possible audience.

“They’re trying to find the perfect Bond for everybody,” he said.

Despite describing the casting as safe, Threlfall says he believes Pattinson has the acting ability to bring something different to the role.

“I like Robert Pattinson as an actor. I think he’s always really interesting. I think he always brings something new to each role he does,” he said. “He’s got a nice intensity about him that Bond should have.”

But Threlfall says the new producers face a bigger challenge than simply choosing the next 007: bringing a character with a complicated history into the modern era.

“He is a problematic hero and he’s a problematic character to teach as well,” he said, pointing to the sexism and misogyny portrayed in earlier Bond films.

“They’ve tried to reform Bond and make him more of a feminist person and everything like that. You can’t get away from the roots of the character.”

Threlfall says some of the films from the 1960s are particularly difficult to watch through a modern lens, raising questions about how the franchise can attract younger audiences while remaining true to its history.

He also expressed disappointment that producers did not choose an actor of colour for the role.

“I was hoping they would finally outgrow that and give us a Bond of colour,” Threlfall said. “But I don’t think the new franchise owners are ready to do that yet.”

Threlfall’s fascination with Bond began in childhood with a toy car and has since grown into an approximately 800-piece collection, along with years spent studying and teaching about the character. In 2015, he taught a writing course at UVic that deconstructed the James Bond film series, examining both its cultural impact and its more controversial themes.

Now, with a new film on the horizon, Threlfall says he hopes to offer another course through the university’s Continuing Studies program.

“Every time there’s a new James Bond film and a new James Bond actor, there’s a renewed interest in the character,” he said.

And while Threlfall grew up watching Sean Connery portray the famous spy, he says Daniel Craig stands out for the emotional depth he brought to the character. As for Pattinson, Threlfall believes the franchise’s enduring appeal will continue to bring audiences back.

“It’s hard to find somebody else in culture who can appeal to such a broad audience over 60-odd years and continually keep them coming back for more.”

BC Hydro is warning the public to stay away from the Puntledge River as a series of powerful storms has pushed the Comox Lake Reservoir above its full level, prompting an increase in water flow from the Comox Dam.

In an update Monday, BC Hydro said it has increased water releases to around 230 cubic metres per second, more than double the amount being released a week earlier.

The increase follows seven days of heavy rainfall that dramatically reversed months of unusually dry conditions in the Comox Valley.

According to BC Hydro, cumulative inflows into the reservoir for November went from record lows to 183 per cent above normal in less than a week.

Daily average inflows reached 350 cubic metres per second on Wednesday last week, a level associated with a one-in-five-year event.

A second surge happened Sunday, when inflows reached 297 cubic metres per second.

BC Hydro says it’s releasing additional water from the dam to lower the reservoir and create room to absorb rainfall from future storms.

Higher-than-normal water releases will continue until the reservoir has lowered sufficiently.

BC Hydro is urging residents and visitors to avoid all sections of the Puntledge River, warning that the high flows create dangerous conditions. Temporary safety signs remain in place along the river.
